name: North Macedonia
summary: North Macedonia had 2,047 battery-electric passenger cars at the end of 2025, about 0.33% of all passenger cars, and no national subsidy for buying an electric car or a home charger was found for 2026. Public charging is mostly provided by EVN Macedonia, whose map lists 12 DC fast-charging sites of up to 180 kW (nine at Makpetrol fuel stations) and more than 40 AC points in 20 towns; residents with an EVN card pay 25/28 MKD per kWh (AC/DC) and other drivers 30/40 MKD by bank card, VAT included. Seven sellers of home chargers were found, mostly in Skopje; some publish device prices of about €440–1,590 per wallbox, none publishes a fixed installation price, and no building-level charging service for apartment blocks was found.

home_companies.name: Polnac.mk (Полнач)
home_companies.city: Skopje (delivery and installation across North Macedonia)
home_companies.what: Sells AC wallboxes for homes and businesses (7.4, 11 and 22 kW, with app) and installs them with certified electricians. Handles the paperwork: technical documentation, application to the distribution operator and the necessary permits. States 500+ installations, 20+ cities served, founded in 2009; 1-year warranty.
home_companies.price: Prices 'from': IGI HS 7.4 kW 33,825 MKD (€550) + 18% VAT = 39,914 MKD; IGI HS 11 kW 42,435 MKD (€690) + 18% VAT = 50,073 MKD; IGI HS 22 kW 45,510 MKD (€740) + 18% VAT = 53,702 MKD. Installation price not published.
home_companies.installation_note: Includes wall mounting, cable to the main distribution board, RCD/MCB protection, earthing and surge protection, final test and user training; 2–4 hours (single-phase), 3–4 hours (three-phase). Free on-site survey in Skopje; outside Skopje for a small travel fee. Free delivery nationwide.

home_companies.name: SWEDCHARGE (North Macedonia)
home_companies.what: Sells Charge Amps home and building chargers (HALO wallbox, AURA twin charger) and a load balancer; offers delivery, mounting and installation, and mentions solutions for collective housing buildings.
home_companies.price: Charge Amps HALO (3.7 / 7.4 / 11 kW, 7.5 m cable): €1,590, summer discount €1,350; Charge Amps AURA (2 × 22 kW): €3,245, summer discount €2,900. VAT not stated; installation extra. No end date given for the discount.

buildings.text: The current text of the Law on Housing could not be retrieved, so the majority needed to install a charger or run a cable through common parts of a multi-unit building is not confirmed here. None of the Macedonian sources checked cites a legal article on chargers in apartment buildings; an installer's guide says the rules in this area 'are still developing'.
buildings.law: Закон за домување (Law on Housing) – article not verified
buildings.source_title: Електричен автомобил во зграда: Како до сопствен полнач во заедничка гаража? | Polnac.mk

buildings.text: Installer guides advise starting with the community of owners (house council) or the building manager, and say their approval is needed to run the cable through common areas. No majority or legal article is cited.

buildings.topic: Who pays and how it is metered
buildings.text: Two set-ups are described: (1) a cable from the resident's own apartment meter, so charging appears on the resident's own EVN bill and can use the cheap tariff; (2) one or two smart chargers on the building's common meter, with RFID cards and a built-in MID-certified meter, where software records each flat's kWh and the manager or house council receives a monthly report to recover the cost from each user.
buildings.source_title: Полнач за електрично возило во зграда: Како да инсталирате Wallbox во подземна или заедничка гаража? | Polnac.mk

buildings.topic: Shared chargers in front of buildings (media)
buildings.text: A specialist portal describes shared smart chargers on a few parking spaces in front of a building, with access limited to residents by RFID card and each resident paying only for the kWh used. It names no legal steps, providers or costs.
buildings.source_title: Заеднички полначи пред зграда: практично решение за станари со ЕВ

buildings.text: Two sellers mention multi-unit buildings: SWEDCHARGE advertises solutions for collective housing buildings with Charge Amps chargers and a load balancer, and eDrive.mk mentions complete solutions for houses and buildings. No company was found that runs shared charging in apartment buildings as a service with metering and billing of residents.

buildings.text: The Energy Law text published on the energy regulator's website (promulgated 21.05.2018) does not mention vehicles or charging points. Later amendments were not checked.

buildings.text: An installer's guide gives typical household connections as 5.7–7.4 kW single-phase (25–32 A) and 11–17.2 kW three-phase (3 × 16 A or 3 × 25 A). More power is requested from EVN's distribution company with an application for connection consent and proof of ownership of the property or parking space.

policy.text: The Transport Community's November 2025 progress report states that none of the Western Balkan partners has yet transposed the EU Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR, 2023/1804), and that Transport Community technical assistance will help them prepare national policy frameworks and identify priority corridors.

The same report names North Macedonia's Ministry of Energy, Mining and Mineral Resources as primarily responsible for alternative-fuels policy, and notes that motor-vehicle tax and registration fees are now linked to measured CO2 emissions (Ministry of Finance).

gaps: Apartment buildings: the text of the Law on Housing was not retrieved (dejure.mk is blocked by robots.txt, pravdiko.mk has an expired security certificate, akademik.mk returned 404), so the co-owner majority for installing a charger in common parts is not confirmed.

Official sites did not load: moepp.gov.mk (environment ministry, timeout), economy.gov.mk (timeout) and ea.gov.mk (Energy Agency, DNS error). 2026 subsidy calls, the National Energy and Climate Plan and any EV targets could not be checked on official pages.

Registrations: no count of new battery-electric cars for 2025 or for 2026 to date was found. The State Statistical Office first-registration table has no fuel breakdown, and Eurostat (new passenger cars by motor energy, updated 01.09.2026) reports only a total of 42,159 for North Macedonia in 2025 with no fuel split; the definitions behind this total and the 'about 6,400 new cars sold' reported by trade media were not checked.

EV fleet figures from the State Statistical Office are quoted from media (CARclub.mk, Denesen.mk); the MakStat table shows values only after an interactive selection that could not be made with the tools used.

Public charge points: no official national count was found. EVN's map gives no total and some sites are listed once per connector, so the EVN figures are approximate; Electromaps (62 stations) is crowd-sourced; chargemap.com is blocked by robots.txt.
EVN's per-kWh prices appear only as an image on emobility.evn.mk/Tariffs.aspx; the figures (25/28 and 30/40 MKD) come from a specialist portal (29.07.2026).
Makpetrol, Charge&GO MK and Orion eMobility publish no per-kWh prices for North Macedonia; whether EVN's tariff applies at Makpetrol stations is not stated.
lawesgo.mk (title 'Electric chargers and cards') did not load (robots.txt timeout); its role (public chargers, cards or sales) is unknown.

Home chargers: loging.mk ('chargers for electric cars' category) returned 403 and e-vozila.apptree.mk did not load; large electronics retailers and car importers' wallbox offers were not checked. Charge&GO MK sells no home chargers locally and links to its Serbian shop (elektropunjaci.com), whose delivery or installation in North Macedonia was not checked.
Installation prices: no company publishes a fixed installation price; the only range (€100–300) comes from an import-advice site without a cited source.
Electricity: no 2026 all-in household price per kWh (energy plus network fees and VAT) was found, and the VAT rate applied to household electricity in 2026 was not confirmed.

Subsidies: no source explicitly confirms or rules out support for home chargers, and municipal schemes (e.g. City of Skopje) were not checked; the September 2025 taxi-subsidy announcement has no published amount, budget or call.
Method: the web-search quota ran out during the check; the remaining items were verified by fetching known URLs only.
